pullRequest.title: Require confirmation before `gh repo delete` deletes private forks
pullRequest.body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to GitHub CLI!

If you are proposing a fix for a security issue, STOP and follow .github/SECURITY.md instead.

Keep the entire pull request self-contained, reviewer-facing, and diegetic: describe the
change, rationale, and evidence within the context of the repository and pull request. Do not
narrate how the pull request was produced or refer to private conversations, prior agent work,
or other behind-the-scenes context. Omit those details unless they materially affect review;
if they do, state the relevant fact and its significance directly.
-->

<!-- List related issues here. Use `fixes` or `closes` keywords to associate an issue number. -->

### Description

<!--
What's the problem? How are we addressing it?

Write for a reviewer who has not worked in this part of the codebase. Give them the
background they need before the problem makes sense, and avoid jargon.
-->

Deleting a private repository also deletes all of its forks ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/deleting-a-repository)). The web UI warns about this before you confirm: "This will also delete all 3 forks since this is a private repository." Our [`repo delete` command](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/f7a06a18a91eef5c0b218b549dab64b86f36f8b9/pkg/cmd/repo/delete/delete.go#L118-L124) doesn't. It only asks you to type the repo name, and `--yes` skips even that.

The person deleting often can't see those forks. Private forks only inherit team access from their upstream, not individual access ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/reference/forks#permissions-of-forks)). 

`gh repo delete` now [looks up the repo](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/4948470b5a97a7fd839df5389527f575070ab2f8/pkg/cmd/repo/delete/http.go#L12-L44) before deleting it. The [new check](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/4948470b5a97a7fd839df5389527f575070ab2f8/pkg/cmd/repo/delete/delete.go#L162-L199) only steps in when the repo takes its forks with it:

```go
// A public repo keeps its forks, and deleting a fork leaves that fork's own forks alone
if !info.Private || info.Fork || info.ForksCount == 0 {
	return nil
}
```

When it does step in:

- In a terminal, `gh` shows the same warning as the web UI, then asks `Delete OWNER/REPO and its forks?`, defaulting to No. It asks even with `--yes`.
- Without a terminal, `gh` exits 1 unless you also pass the new `--accept-cascading-deletion-of-private-forks` flag.

### How did you test this change?

<!--
Report only actions you actually performed and results you actually observed, using factual
first-person language (for example, "I ran..." and "I saw..."). Do not present planned,
hypothetical, inferred, or merely expected scenarios as testing.

Automated test results do not belong here. Passing unit tests, `go test ./...` output, and
coverage numbers tell a reviewer nothing they cannot see from CI, so do not paste them.

If you did not exercise the changed behavior, write `Not tested` and explain why.

Use one or more of these, whichever communicates best:

1. Screenshots or GIFs of the real command running. Preferred whenever the change is visible
   in terminal output. If output changed, show it before and after.
2. Given/When/Then scenarios, but only when you actually executed the steps. For example:
   Given I was in a repo with no open pull requests
   When I ran `gh pr list`
   Then I saw "no open pull requests in cli/cli"
3. A natural language walkthrough of what you did by hand, the states you covered, and what
   you saw, including error and edge cases.

If you leave this empty, your pull request will very likely be closed.
-->

I built `gh` from trunk at f7a06a1 and from this branch at 4948470. I pointed both at a small local stand-in for the REST API through an HTTP proxy, so no real repositories were touched. Every run used an empty config directory and a placeholder token.

I recorded four terminal runs of this branch's build. Each one ends by printing the requests the stand-in API received.

- With 3 forks, I saw the warning, answered `y`, and typed the repo name. The API saw the GET, then the DELETE.
- Pressing Enter at the fork prompt took the default No. `gh` exited with status 2 and sent no DELETE.
- With `--yes`, the fork prompt still appeared, but the name prompt didn't.
- With the new flag, only the name prompt appeared, and the API saw only the DELETE.

Without a terminal, trunk deleted a private repo with 3 forks and printed nothing. This branch exited with status 1 after only the GET:

```
--accept-cascading-deletion-of-private-forks required when not running interactively: deleting octo-org/secrets-vault will also delete all 3 forks since this is a private repository
```

I also ran these without a terminal:

- Adding the new flag skipped the lookup and sent only the DELETE.
- An internal repo with forks got the same error as a private one.
- A public repo with forks, a private fork with forks, and a private repo with no forks were still deleted.
- A missing repo and a renamed repo printed byte-identical output on both builds, with the same exit code. That includes the `delete_repo` scope hint for the missing repo. The branch now stops at the GET, so no DELETE is sent.

I also ran four acceptance scripts from this branch against the `gh-acceptance-testing` org, using a GitHub App installation token. All four passed:

- The new `repo-delete-private-forks` script forks a private repo within the org. `gh repo delete --yes` exited with the new error and left the repo in place. With the new flag, it was deleted.
- `repo-delete` still deleted a private repo with no forks.
- `repo-fork-sync` and `pr-view-same-org-fork` each deleted a private fork, then deleted its parent with the new flag.

### Key points

<!--
Tradeoffs you accepted, alternatives you rejected, and anything a reviewer would otherwise have to guess at.
-->

- `--yes` still only skips typing the name. You pass it before seeing the fork count, so I don't think it counts as agreeing to lose the forks. Automation that runs `gh` with a terminal attached, like `ssh -t` or `docker run -it`, will now stop at the fork prompt unless it passes the new flag.
- `forks_count` counts forks you can't see. It also counts forks of forks, which I checked on two public repos where a fork had its own fork. So the count should match the web UI's.
- If the lookup fails, nothing is deleted. The new flag skips the lookup entirely, so it gets you the old behavior exactly.
- The lookup uses REST with the same scope hint and redirect policy as the DELETE. GraphQL would have changed the error for a missing repo.
- Like `--yes`, the new flag is ignored when no repo argument is given.
- 16 acceptance scripts fork a private repo and clean up the upstream with `gh repo delete --yes`. I added the new flag there. Otherwise that cleanup fails if the fork's own cleanup never ran.

### Notes for reviewers

<!--
Where should review start, and what should be read next? Call out anything you are unsure about.

Link related issues or prior discussion, with one sentence on why each matters.
-->

- Start with the [new check](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/4948470b5a97a7fd839df5389527f575070ab2f8/pkg/cmd/repo/delete/delete.go#L162-L199), then the [lookup](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/4948470b5a97a7fd839df5389527f575070ab2f8/pkg/cmd/repo/delete/http.go#L12-L44). The new cases in `TestNewCmdDelete` and `Test_deleteRun` cover each branch.
- I'm not sure how quickly `forks_count` drops after a fork is deleted. That's part of why the acceptance cleanup passes the flag instead of relying on the fork being deleted first.
- The 9 changed acceptance scripts that fork into a personal account need a user token, so I didn't run them.

nodes.body:
🛑 Requirement: Poll for the fork count instead of using a fixed sleep

If GitHub takes more than five seconds to update the upstream's fork count, this test fails before exercising either deletion path. Replace the sleep and one-shot lookup with bounded polling until the count is 1, failing on timeout before attempting deletion. This follows the condition-based wait requirement in .github/skills/writing-acceptance-tests/SKILL.md:94-96 and the existing wait-for-repository-ready helper pattern.
I mean, yeah but this is a problem with a bunch of tests already so gonna leave it

commit.messageHeadline: Require confirmation before deleting a private repo's forks
Accept cascading fork deletion in acceptance cleanup
Add acceptance test for deleting a private repo with forks
